anchors.name: The Alpha
anchors.description: Needs hierarchy and control; the wolf enforces the order the character demands.
anchors.recoverOne: Put order ahead of independent reasoning.
anchors.recoverAll: Use the force of the wolf to bring subordinates into line.

anchors.name: The Challenger
anchors.description: Refuses second place and turns to overwhelming force to establish superiority.
anchors.recoverOne: Disregard safety and reason to appear superior.
anchors.recoverAll: Use Kuruth or the hunt to dominate a rival.

anchors.name: The Destroyer
anchors.description: Pursues goals through devastation, leaving destruction in the wake of every achievement.
anchors.recoverOne: Inflict substantial, lasting damage while pursuing success.
anchors.recoverAll: Surrender to Kuruth without considering other approaches.

anchors.name: The Fox
anchors.description: Survives through cunning, retreat and patience, even when the pack expects a fight.
anchors.recoverOne: Abandon everything and flee the scene.
anchors.recoverAll: Enter Kuruth while escaping a violent situation.

anchors.name: The Monster
anchors.description: Breaks prey psychologically through terror and shock before making the killing strike.
anchors.recoverOne: Frighten or disgust someone into submission.
anchors.recoverAll: Use the hunt or Kuruth as a means of terror.

anchors.name: The Soldier
anchors.description: Follows the alpha's orders as a weapon of the pack, placing the plan ahead of personal safety.
anchors.recoverOne: Disregard personal safety to carry out a leader's order.
anchors.recoverAll: Undertake a hunt or enter Kuruth to obey the alpha against personal good judgment.

anchors.name: Community Organizer
anchors.description: Works through relationships, groups and institutions rather than relying on one person's force.
anchors.recoverOne: Persuade a group to address its internal problems before outside ones.
anchors.recoverAll: Persuade the pack to forgo a hunt in favor of a social or political solution.

anchors.name: Cub
anchors.description: Relies on others' guidance and support rather than taking full responsibility for every decision.
anchors.recoverOne: Follow another person's advice instead of personal impulses.
anchors.recoverAll: Entrust life and limb completely to someone else when the wolf's power could accomplish the goal.

anchors.name: Guru
anchors.description: Shares practical wisdom and guides others toward workable answers.
anchors.recoverOne: Someone succeeds by following the character's advice.
anchors.recoverAll: Practical advice leads the pack to a solution other than the hunt.

anchors.name: Hedonist
anchors.description: Seeks answers in immediate pleasure and personal gratification.
anchors.recoverOne: Choose personal indulgence instead of greater success.
anchors.recoverAll: Abandon the hunt for personal pursuits.

anchors.name: Lone Wolf
anchors.description: Prefers to handle a problem alone when individual action seems the best solution.
anchors.recoverOne: Act independently of the pack to solve a pack problem.
anchors.recoverAll: Undermine the pack's plans and solve the problem alone while the pack is hunting.

anchors.name: Wallflower
anchors.description: Avoids the spotlight, solving problems through subtlety, restraint and quiet action.
anchors.recoverOne: Work from the shadows, outside the attention attracted by the pack.
anchors.recoverAll: Operate independently to complement the pack while it is hunting.

breakingPoints.description: Defiling a locus.
Refusing to participate in Siskur-Dah.
Remaining outside the Hisil for a week.
Using a silver weapon against another werewolf.
Violating the Oath of the Moon (Forsaken only).
Remaining outside the Hisil for a month.
Allowing a spirit safe passage into the physical world.
Eating processed food.
Mating with a human.
Remaining outside the Hisil for a day.
Killing a human or wolf.
Remaining in the Hisil for a week.
Hunting humans or wolves for food.
Killing a packmate.
Eating human or wolf flesh for Essence.
Remaining in the Hisil for a month.
Inflicting Lunacy on a loved one.
Leading the Siskur-Dah.
Spending more than two days away from the pack.
Remaining in the Hisil for a full day.

fields.label: Blood
fields.text: Making a clearly bad choice in the heat of the moment that expresses Blood restores one spent Willpower. Giving in to Kuruth or declaring a hunt on impulse in accordance with Blood restores all spent Willpower.

fields.label: Bone
fields.text: Suppressing rage and acting according to a fundamental belief that expresses Bone restores one spent Willpower. Standing firm and letting reason interfere with the hunt or cause conflict within the pack restores all spent Willpower.

fields.label: Custom anchors
fields.text: The six examples of each kind are not exhaustive. Custom Blood and Bone need agreed situations for restoring one point and for restoring all spent Willpower.

fields.label: Physical Touchstone
fields.text: A person, place, object or ideal that anchors the werewolf to flesh and humanity. While accessible, it grants +2 dice to resist a breaking point toward Spirit. It cannot be accessed at Harmony 2 or lower.

fields.label: Spiritual Touchstone
fields.text: A spirit, totem, locus or philosophy that draws the werewolf to the Hisil. While accessible, it grants +2 dice to resist a breaking point toward Flesh. It cannot be accessed at Harmony 8 or higher.

fields.label: Loss and replacement
fields.text: Losing a physical Touchstone moves Harmony one step toward Spirit; losing a spiritual Touchstone moves it one step toward Flesh. Establishing a replacement is a breaking point in the opposite direction.

fields.label: Willpower
fields.text: A meaningful interaction that reinforces the bond restores one spent Willpower. Risking the character's life or pack to defend the relationship can restore all spent Willpower.

fields.label: Bashing damage
fields.text: Regenerate bashing damage each turn at the rate shown by Primal Urge. This is at least one point per turn.

fields.label: Lethal damage
fields.text: Regenerate one lethal damage every 15 minutes. Spending one Essence reflexively changes that turn's regeneration from bashing to lethal.

fields.label: Aggravated damage
fields.text: Regenerate one aggravated damage every four days. Only silver and supernatural powers cause aggravated damage directly; mundane harm that would be aggravated to a human is lethal to an Uratha. Lethal damage can still roll over into aggravated damage.

fields.label: Gauru
fields.text: Heal all bashing and lethal damage at the start of every turn in Gauru.

fields.label: Tilts
fields.text: A Tilt caused by an aggravated wound, such as a lost arm or eye, heals when the associated wound heals.

fields.label: Toxins
fields.text: Subtract Primal Urge from the Toxicity of a poison or disease.

fields.label: Witnesses
fields.text: Witnessing lethal regeneration causes Lunacy as if the werewolf were in Dalu, regardless of the actual form.

fields.label: Human senses
fields.text: The First Change corrects existing sensory impairments, including congenital blindness or deafness, and regenerates lost sense organs within days. Human senses are the default in Hishu and Dalu. Choosing other senses is a reflexive action without a roll.

fields.label: Wolf senses
fields.text: Default in Urshul and Urhan. Apply the form's wolf-sense Perception bonus. Other senses compensate for sensory deprivation, negating its penalties.

fields.label: Smell
fields.text: Primal Urge can identify a remembered character without a roll even through concealment or disguise. Wits + Primal Urge links another Uratha to a previously smelled scene; deliberately left scent needs no roll. Identifying Uratha or Wolf-Blooded by smell requires Wits + Primal Urge, an instant action and close personal proximity.

fields.label: Hearing
fields.text: Range is one mile (about two kilometers) per Primal Urge dot. Ignore penalties for quiet sounds or hearing range and hear frequencies unavailable to human ears. Urban noise usually limits distinguishable sounds to the immediate surroundings.

fields.label: Vision
fields.text: Halve darkness penalties, rounded down, and ignore vision penalties for rapid movement. Wolf vision distinguishes fewer colors than human vision.

fields.label: Blood trail
fields.text: Tasting a living creature's blood reveals its exact direction at any distance, not a safe route or the distance itself. Only one victim can be followed. The link ends after a lunar month or when another creature's blood is tasted.

fields.label: Spirit senses
fields.text: Send the current form's default senses across the Gauntlet in either direction with an instant action, or reflexively for one Essence. Without a Gift, each sense works on one side only. Splitting senses between worlds gives −2 to actions involving Perception or concentration and removes compensation for sensory penalties. Apply the Gauntlet's dice modifier to Perception. Spirits in Twilight are sensed without focusing unless they intentionally hide.

fields.label: Harmony 9–10
fields.text: Changing form costs one Essence and an instant action. Clothes and belongings do not transform with the werewolf.

fields.label: Harmony 7–8
fields.text: Change form reflexively for one Essence, or as an instant action at no cost.

fields.label: Harmony 4–6
fields.text: Change form reflexively without Essence or a roll.

fields.label: Harmony 2–3
fields.text: Prevent a change reflexively for one Essence, or as an instant action at no cost.

fields.label: Harmony 0–1
fields.text: Prevent a change with one Essence and an instant action.

fields.label: Low Harmony
fields.text: Must change at least once each scene; Essence may prevent it only when not stressed. In combat, a chase or another threatening situation, shift one form each turn toward the appropriate form: Urhan to flee, Hishu to hide or Gauru to fight. Stress prevents resisting this movement.

fields.label: Belongings
fields.text: Below Harmony 9, clothing and immediate possessions transform with the character, stretching for Dalu or merging into the body in Gauru, Urshul and Urhan as appropriate to the scene.

fields.label: Bites
fields.text: Bites in every form count as mystical damage sources against creatures vulnerable to such sources. Even a Hishu bite deals lethal damage to vampires.

fields.label: Dice Pool
fields.text: Power Attribute + appropriate Skill + Auspice Renown, contested by the prey's Composure + Primal Urge; instant action. Use Strength for physical pursuit, Presence for a staredown or Intelligence to outwit the prey. The Skill follows the interaction, not a single mandatory pool.

fields.label: Success
fields.text: Inflict the Auspice's Hunter's Aspect Condition for the scene; exceptional success lasts one day per Primal Urge dot. Expiration alone gives no Beat. Only one Hunter's Aspect Condition can affect a character at once; further attempts fail while it remains.

fields.label: Auspices
fields.text: Cahalith: Resigned (Monstrous). Elodoth: Isolated (Isolating). Irraka: Unaware (Blissful). Ithaeur: Mystified (Mystic). Rahu: Submissive (Dominant). The aspect can affect humans, spirits, Uratha and other supernatural creatures.

fields.label: Advancement
fields.text: A deed worthy of Renown permits a purchase for three Experiences per dot; categories are Cunning, Glory, Honor, Purity and Wisdom, capped at five each. Raising Auspice Renown grants the next Facet of the own Moon Gift. Raising another category grants an appropriate Facet of an unlocked Shadow Gift or a Wolf Gift.

fields.label: Effective Spirit Rank
fields.text: Total Renown 0–3: Rank 1; 4–7: Rank 2; 8–12: Rank 3; 13–18: Rank 4; 19 or more: Rank 5.

fields.label: Spirit brands
fields.text: Once per story, spend one Essence to intensify the spirit brands, making them faintly visible in the physical world. Spirits, Uratha, Wolf-Blooded and others attuned to the spirit world intuitively recognize the Renown and its deeds. Choose a category to receive its Renown Condition at that rating: Cunning, Glorious, Honorable, Pure or Wise. Displaying the brands invites challenges.

fields.label: Limits
fields.text: Primal Urge sets the maximum reserve and expenditure per turn. When an effect costs more than the per-turn limit, spend the required Essence across multiple turns; the effect activates after the full cost is paid.

fields.label: Loci
fields.text: Absorb Essence at the heart of a locus in the Hisil; in the physical world, consume the unusual meat or vegetation that appears nearby.

fields.label: Siskur-Dah
fields.text: The Sacred Hunt rite permits hunting and devouring spirits in the Hisil to take their Essence.

fields.label: Human or wolf flesh
fields.text: Choose to consume flesh for one Essence per point of damage dealt by a bite. Devouring flesh for Essence causes aggravated wounds, violates the Oath of the Moon and always causes a breaking point toward Spirit.

fields.label: Other sources
fields.text: Destroying a fetish releases its stored Essence to the werewolf. The first sight of the character's Auspice moon each night grants one Essence.

fields.label: Uses
fields.text: Essence fuels Gifts and fetishes, changes regeneration to lethal, speeds Reaching and pays shapeshifting costs when Harmony requires them.

fields.label: Feeding
fields.text: The Primal Urge table sets the food required for nourishment. Other food can be swallowed but does not nourish the werewolf. Each day without the required food loses one Essence. At the highest levels, nourishment requires spirit ephemera or human or wolf flesh.

fields.label: Hunt interval
fields.text: Exceeding the table's interval without Siskur-Dah loses one Essence each day and causes a breaking point toward Flesh.

fields.label: Dice Pool
fields.text: To enter Spirit, roll 10 − Harmony; to enter Flesh, roll Harmony. Apply the Gauntlet's dice modifier. A locus is normally required. Harmony 3 or lower needs no locus to enter Spirit; Harmony 8 or higher needs no locus to enter Flesh. Harmony 10 cannot enter Spirit; Harmony 0 cannot enter Flesh.

fields.label: Transition
fields.text: Crossing takes two turns per level of Gauntlet strength. The character vanishes at the start and appears on the other side at the end. Exceptional success or spending one Essence makes the crossing immediate.

fields.label: Suggested modifiers
fields.text: Looking into a reflective surface +1; entering Shadow by day −2; entering Flesh by day +2.

fields.label: Gauntlet
fields.text: Dense urban areas: strength 5, modifier −3. Suburbs or towns: 4/−2. Small towns or villages: 3/−1. Wilderness or countryside: 2/0. Locus: 1/+2. Verge: 0, modifier not applicable. These are guidelines; local conditions can vary.

fields.label: Damage
fields.text: Silver weapons always inflict aggravated damage. Non-damaging contact causes intense pain and lasting scars like aggravated wounds, but no damage.

fields.label: Material
fields.text: Use real metallic silver, not compounds such as silver nitrate. Alloys and mixtures must contain at least 80% silver. A silver coating works for one damaging hit. Unless forged from silver, the weapon is improvised.

fields.label: Witnesses
fields.text: Close witnesses of Dalu, Gauru or Urshul, of shapeshifting or of regeneration suffer a breaking point at an appropriate moment. Wolf-Blooded and creatures without Integrity, including Uratha, vampires and spirits, are immune.

fields.label: Modifiers
fields.text: Apply the Primal Urge Lunacy penalty. Dalu gives the witness +2; Gauru gives −2; Urshul has no additional form modifier. A witness dealt lethal damage by the werewolf gains +1 and adds, rather than subtracts, wound penalties. Witnesses working together gain +1 for two, +2 for a small group (about five or fewer), +3 for up to ten, or +4 for a larger crowd.

fields.label: Success
fields.text: Gain Guilty, Shaken or Spooked and suffer −2 to all actions for the scene; events are likely rationalized. Exceptional success gives no Condition or action penalty, restores all spent Willpower and preserves an accurate memory.

fields.label: Failure
fields.text: Lose one Integrity and gain Atavism, Delusion or Reception as appropriate; flee or panic, then rationalize the memory. The Lunacy Condition expires without a Beat after days equal to the werewolf's Primal Urge if unresolved. Dramatic failure starts becoming Wolf-Blooded at a moon phase during the next lunar month, tending toward the witnessed werewolf's Auspice.

fields.label: Entry
fields.text: A Kuruth trigger normally begins Wasu-Im. Taking Gauru during it, or being triggered while already in Gauru, immediately begins Basu-Im.

fields.label: Wasu-Im
fields.text: Immediately take Dalu or Urshul and remain there. As with Gauru's Rage, resisting the urge to attack requires Resolve + Composure; failure starts Basu-Im. Instead of attacking, an instant Resolve + Composure action grants one lucid turn per success. Exceptional success ends Wasu-Im. Harmony sets the time before Basu-Im; voluntary entry is possible at any time.

fields.label: Basu-Im
fields.text: Immediately take Gauru for the Primal Urge table's minimum duration, even if Gauru was already used that scene; ignore the usual form duration and wound penalties. Attempts to influence, intimidate or divert the werewolf by any means take −2 × Primal Urge, in addition to supernatural tolerance. Gauru's Rage applies against everyone except other werewolves in Basu-Im. Without prey, destroy property until fresh prey is found.

fields.label: Contagion within the pack
fields.text: Werewolf packmates within 10 yards who see or smell the raging character enter Basu-Im after one turn. Resolve + Composure can resist, requiring one success per character currently in Kuruth in the scene; roll again whenever another packmate enters Basu-Im.

fields.label: Afterward
fields.text: After the minimum Basu-Im time, collapse into Hishu with no memory of the events. Learning what happened may cause a breaking point toward Spirit.

fields.label: Categories
fields.text: Each character has passive, common and specific triggers. Passive triggers occur without awareness; common triggers require witnessing or sensing the circumstance; specific triggers are rarer events. Harmony selects the applicable category; at Harmony 5 no personal trigger applies.

fields.label: Blood (passive / common / specific)
fields.text: Smelling human blood / tasting human blood / swallowing human blood.

fields.label: Moon (passive / common / specific)
fields.text: The Auspice moon is in the sky / see it in the sky / hear a wolf or werewolf howl while it is in the sky.

fields.label: The Other (passive / common / specific)
fields.text: A supernatural creature comes within 10 yards / witness one do something obviously inhuman / become the target of a supernatural power.

fields.label: Pack (passive / common / specific)
fields.text: A packmate suffers lethal damage / see someone attack a packmate / cause lethal damage to a packmate.

fields.label: Territory (passive / common / specific)
fields.text: An unfamiliar werewolf enters the territory without permission / see an unfamiliar werewolf there / an unfamiliar werewolf challenges the pack's ability to do its duty.

fields.label: Wounds (passive / common / specific)
fields.text: Be in a Wound's area / interact with a Wound-born spirit / be attacked by a Wound-born spirit.

fields.label: General triggers
fields.text: All Uratha also risk Kuruth from staying in Gauru too long, taking Gauru outside combat, suffering silver damage or being forced into Kuruth by an Elodoth. These general triggers cannot be opted out of by choosing personal triggers.

fields.label: Balance
fields.text: Harmony ranges from 0 (Spirit) to 10 (Flesh), with balance at 5 and a starting rating of 7. Experiences cannot raise or lower it.

fields.label: Dice Pool
fields.text: Resolve + Composure; Willpower cannot modify this pool. Apply the specific breaking point's modifier. Toward Spirit, subtract one die per Harmony below 5; failure reduces Harmony by one. Toward Flesh, subtract one die per Harmony above 5; failure increases Harmony by one. An accessible appropriate Touchstone normally adds +2.

fields.label: Bans
fields.text: Harmony 4 or lower imposes persistent Ban Conditions: one at 4–3, two at 2, three at 1, four at 0. Raising Harmony enough resolves the excess bans; the player chooses which to discard.

fields.label: Personal breaking points
fields.text: The listed events are a starting point, not an exhaustive list. Player and Storyteller should define one or two personal breaking points in each direction based on Auspice, Tribe and Touchstones.
